title: Haus on 15: flexible layouts in the heart of SS15.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #480 | HAUS ON 15, SUBANG JAYA
excerpt: A freehold redevelopment beside INTI in SS15, with two towers for sale, a student-housing tower and shops. Sean likes the split entrances, the dual-key and tri-key layouts and the pricing, but sees it as an investment rather than a family home.
takeaways: Two residential towers of 522 units, a separate student-housing tower and 18 shops on 2.88 acres.
About RM950 psf freehold, with studios, dual-keys and tri-keys for room-by-room letting.
SS15 is busy all day, and the residents will be mostly students and young adults.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Haus on 15 is a redevelopment of 2.88 acres: Towers A and B, 522 units for sale, a third tower of student housing for Taylor's with no access to the residents' facilities, and 18 shops facing the street. The public drop-off serves the shops, while residents use a separate entrance on the quiet side and a car park ramp split so one turn climbs two floors.

Units run from a 690 sq ft two-bedroom to a 980 sq ft tri-key of three studios, which sold fastest. Sean viewed the 960 sq ft dual-key show unit: a studio with its own bathroom and a pantry already plumbed, beside a two-bedroom unit with a kitchen, yard and shared bathroom.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It sits beside INTI's Subang campus on the edge of SS15, between the shops and the terrace houses, next to Sri KL school and opposite Subang Jaya Medical Centre. The NPE, Federal Highway and KESAS are close, and SS15 LRT station is about a 10-minute walk, on the Kelana Jaya line straight to KLCC. The streets around are packed with students, cafes and illegal parking most of the day.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: The freehold units sell for about RM950 psf, with Block A at a premium over Block B, so the dual-key comes to about RM900,000-plus. The Grand at SS15 nearby already transacts at about RM900 to RM1,000 psf, even at auction, and lets rooms for about RM1,000 a month. Student rooms near Taylor's cost about RM1,200 to RM1,500 even for twin sharing, and units here can be let whole, split in two or room by room.

standout.title: Two front doors
standout.body: The busy street side gets an open drop-off that feeds the shops, while residents come and go through a separate private entrance on the quiet residential side. A car park ramp that splits at each turn gets them to their bays quickly without the long run a full speed ramp would need.

pros: The SS15 location: Subang Jaya now has city status and good highway links, the LRT is a 10-minute walk on a line that runs straight to KLCC, and the project sits on the fringe between quiet terrace houses and the commercial hub, getting the benefits of both.

Design that reads the site: a public entrance for the shops and a private one for residents, a split ramp, 18 shops continuing the SS15 street, a student tower kept apart from the residents' facilities, and layouts from studios to dual-keys and tri-keys for every kind of tenant.

Scarcity and pricing: new projects like this are running out in Subang Jaya, yet the developer priced cautiously against nearby projects, so the rental numbers make sense; Block B was fully booked quickly.
cons: It is investment-driven: with a student tower and mostly students and young adults in the other two, it suits a young couple without children better than a family, and Sean doesn't understand the many children's facilities on the deck.
SS15 is busy all day, with double parking, honking and school pick-up jams at the roundabout by Sri KL, so residents driving in will often need the alternative route via SS16.

The density looks alarming to long-time residents used to landed homes, though about 500 units on 2.88 acres is reasonable for the area. Freehold land in Subang is almost gone, and investors should check rents and transacted prices nearby rather than fear oversupply.

closing: An investment-led project in a hub that never sleeps; Sean, whose child will study in the area, says it makes a lot of sense for parents with school years ahead.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team, whom Sean calls friends, showed him the sales gallery and show unit; the finishes shown may differ from the actual units. Sean says his own child will go to school in the area.
